meta_desc: Class 1 Fun with Numbers worksheet (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 8): tens and ones, numbers to 99, comparing, before and after, 10 more and 10 less. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Compare the tens first, then the ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Group objects in tens: 4 tens and 7 ones make 47.
  • To compare, look at the tens: 52 > 48 because 5 tens is more than 4 tens.
  • 10 more changes the tens digit: 36 → 46.

Examples

Example

What is 6 tens and 3 ones?

60 + 3

Answer: 63

Example

Which is bigger: 39 or 41?

4 tens is more than 3 tens

Answer: 41

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 6 tens 3 ones as 36Tens come first: 63.
Comparing ones firstCompare the tens digit first.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Count the rods by tens: 10, 20, 30. Count the cubes: 1, 2, 3, 4. 3 tens and 4 ones is 34.
Each rod is 1 ten. Count the rods: there are 6 tens.

items.q: How many ones are there?
items.e: Each small cube is 1 one. Count the cubes: there are 8 ones.
Count the rods by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Count the cubes: 1, 2, 3, 4. 5 tens and 4 ones is 54.
A rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 one. There are 8 rods and 7 cubes: 8 tens and 7 ones.

items.e: A rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 one. There are 3 rods and 7 cubes: 3 tens and 7 ones.

items.q: In which number does the 5 mean 5 tens?
items.e: The tens digit is the first digit. In 56 the 5 is first, so it means 5 tens. In the other numbers the 5 is in the ones place.

items.q: In which number does the 3 mean 3 tens?
items.e: The tens digit is the first digit. In 35 the 3 is first, so it means 3 tens. In the other numbers the 3 is in the ones place.
In 54 the 5 is in the tens place. 54 is 5 tens and 4 ones.

items.q: Which shows 27?
items.e: 27 is 2 tens and 7 ones. That is 20 + 7.
74 is 7 tens and 4 ones. That is 70 + 4.

items.q: Which shows 38?
items.e: 38 is 3 tens and 8 ones. That is 30 + 8.
67 is 6 tens and 7 ones. That is 60 + 7.

items.q: 82 = ☐ + 2
items.e: 82 is 8 tens and 2 ones. 8 tens is 80. So 82 = 80 + 2.

items.q: 41 = ☐ + 1
items.e: 41 is 4 tens and 1 one. 4 tens is 40. So 41 = 40 + 1.

items.q: 37 = 30 + ☐
items.e: 37 is 3 tens and 7 ones. The tens make 30. The ones make 7. So 37 = 30 + 7.
Break 1 ten into 10 ones. 40 + 11 = 51. It is still 51.

items.q: Which is another way to make 28?
items.e: Break 1 ten into 10 ones. 10 + 18 = 28. It is still 28.

items.q: 34 = 20 + ☐
items.e: Break 1 ten into 10 ones. 3 tens and 4 ones becomes 2 tens and 14 ones. So 34 = 20 + 14.
Look at the tens first. 52 has 5 tens and 25 has 2 tens. 5 tens is more than 2 tens, so 52 > 25. The ones do not matter.
Both have 3 tens. Look at the ones. 34 has 4 ones and 39 has 9 ones. 9 ones is more than 4 ones, so 34 < 39.

Look at the tens first. 57 has 5 tens and 75 has 7 tens. 7 tens is more than 5 tens, so 57 < 75. The ones do not matter.

30 + 6 is 3 tens and 6 ones. That is 36. Both sides are the same number, so use =. 63 is 6 tens and 3 ones, not the same.

items.q: The alligator mouth opens toward the greater number. What does the picture say?
items.e: The alligator mouth opens toward the greater number. Here it opens toward 65. Look at the tens first. 65 has 6 tens and 56 has 5 tens. 6 tens is more than 5 tens, so 65 > 56. The ones do not matter. The picture says 65 is greater than 56.

items.q: The alligator mouth opens toward the greater number. What does the picture say?
items.e: The alligator mouth opens toward the greater number. Here it opens toward 83. Look at the tens first. 38 has 3 tens and 83 has 8 tens. 8 tens is more than 3 tens, so 38 < 83. The ones do not matter. The picture says 38 is less than 83.
A has 4 tens and 0 ones: 40. B has 5 tens and 4 ones: 54. Look at the tens first. 40 has 4 tens and 54 has 5 tens. 5 tens is more than 4 tens, so 40 < 54. 54 is the greater number.

items.q: What number does each group show? Which number is less?
items.e: A has 2 tens and 1 one: 21. B has 1 ten and 8 ones: 18. Look at the tens first. 21 has 2 tens and 18 has 1 ten. 2 tens is more than 1 ten, so 21 > 18. The ones do not matter. 18 has more blocks, but each ten is worth 10 ones. 18 is the smaller number.
A has 7 tens and 3 ones: 73. B has 7 tens and 6 ones: 76. Both have 7 tens. Look at the ones. 73 has 3 ones and 76 has 6 ones. 6 ones is more than 3 ones, so 73 < 76. 76 is the greater number.

items.q: What number does each group show? Which number is less?
items.e: A has 4 tens and 5 ones: 45. B has 3 tens and 7 ones: 37. Look at the tens first. 45 has 4 tens and 37 has 3 tens. 4 tens is more than 3 tens, so 45 > 37. The ones do not matter. 37 is the smaller number.

A has 8 tens and 5 ones: 85. B has 5 tens and 8 ones: 58. Look at the tens first. 85 has 8 tens and 58 has 5 tens. 8 tens is more than 5 tens, so 85 > 58. The ones do not matter. The same digits in a different order make a different number. 85 is the greater number.

A has 4 tens and 6 ones: 46. B has 5 tens and 3 ones: 53. Look at the tens first. 46 has 4 tens and 53 has 5 tens. 5 tens is more than 4 tens, so 46 < 53. The ones do not matter. 46 has more blocks, but each ten is worth 10 ones. 46 is the smaller number.
A has 8 tens and 1 one: 81. B has 8 tens and 0 ones: 80. Both have 8 tens. Look at the ones. 81 has 1 one and 80 has 0 ones. 1 one is more than 0 ones, so 81 > 80. 81 is the greater number.

items.q: What number does each group show? Which number is less?
items.e: A has 3 tens and 4 ones: 34. B has 1 ten and 7 ones: 17. Look at the tens first. 34 has 3 tens and 17 has 1 ten. 3 tens is more than 1 ten, so 34 > 17. The ones do not matter. 17 is the smaller number.
